A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dyn-HaMR. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments, component and initialization ablations, plausibility evaluations and runtime measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds quantitative and qualitative evaluations on Ego-Exo4D and HOT3D, including an acceleration analysis.

M1.justification: The three-stage pipeline, motion prior, SLAM-based optimization and interaction losses remain unchanged. Appendix A.1 newly documents initialization filters for hallucinated detections; this additional implementation description does not establish a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds actual evaluations on Ego-Exo4D hand ego-pose recordings and HOT3D head-mounted hand/object recordings, substantially extending empirical coverage. The original H2O, HOI4D, FPHA, EgoDexter, InterHand2.6M and web-video evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Existing comparison methods are retained. v3 adds HaMeR + DPVO to the Ego-Exo4D and HOT3D comparisons in Tables 4–5 and Figure 11, providing a focused baseline that combines hand reconstruction with camera tracking.

E3.justification: The added benchmarks use validation splits because test annotations are unavailable. Ego-Exo4D omits acceleration error because its annotations are too sparse, while HOT3D includes an alternative calculation with time-step division. Existing 128-frame evaluation and alignment settings remain.

E4.justification: v3 adds a focused sensitivity analysis comparing HOT3D acceleration errors with and without time-step normalization in Table 7. Earlier component, initialization, long-sequence and plausibility analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new acceleration comparison concerns metric computation, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: All eight original numerical tables retain their values after matching renumbering. Substantial new results appear in v3 Tables 4–5 and 7 and Figure 11. For example, G-MPJPE is 53.89 versus 213.75 for HaMeR + DPVO on Ego-Exo4D, and 42.36 versus 129.45 on HOT3D. These are new evaluations, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical model and optimization objectives remain equivalent. Appendix B supplies standard calculations for existing evaluation metrics; it adds no substantive theoretical result or proof. The former Equation 14 is retained inline.

C1.justification: The introduction changes its contribution from 'Proposing' a data-driven hand motion prior to 'Leveraging' one, narrowing the novelty claim. The central claims about dynamic-camera global hand reconstruction and superior reconstruction performance remain.

C2.justification: v3 newly explains how overlapping detections and occasional handedness errors produce HaMeR hallucinations, and explains why sparse Ego-Exo4D annotations prevent meaningful acceleration-error evaluation. Existing interpretations and long-sequence limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds overlap-filtering, short-detection removal and handedness-invalidation thresholds. Appendix B specifies Umeyama alignment and trajectory/acceleration calculations. These improve documentation without establishing changes to existing experiments; optimization hyperparameters, hardware and runtime information remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to HOT3D, Ego-Exo4D, NRDF and SignAvatars. Related work briefly discusses SignAvatars, future work references NRDF, and the contribution wording more clearly acknowledges use of an existing motion prior.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained. v3 makes localized contribution, related-work and results edits, adds acknowledgments, introduces Appendix B for evaluation metrics, renames the former experimental appendix C and moves the occlusion discussion within Appendix A.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 4, 5 and 7 and Figure 11, substantially expanding the empirical displays. It moves Table 1, relocates Figure 4's third example into appendix Figure 7, enlarges the trajectory plots in Figure 6 and compresses/rearranges other appendix displays. Relocated examples are not new results.

improvement.justification: The added HaMeR + DPVO comparisons better test the value of Dyn-HaMR beyond combining existing components, while two additional benchmarks and implementation details strengthen validation and reproducibility. The gains are focused: the original evidence remains unchanged, and Appendix B/Table 7 still contain inconsistent acceleration notation and units. Overall, v3 provides a useful but limited quality improvement.
